question: Why is it important to maintain a space cushion between your vehicle and others?
options: a:It allows you time to react to unexpected situations.,b:It prevents distractions from other vehicles.,c:It keeps traffic flowing at a faster pace.
note: Leaving plenty of space around your vehicle gives you the time and room to react to mistakes or sudden actions by other drivers.

question: What is the 'No zone' around large trucks or buses?
options: a:The vehicle’s blind spots where smaller vehicles may not be seen.,b:A speed limit zone for trucks.,c:A restricted audio zone for loud stereos.
note: A truck or bus has blind spots in the front, rear, and on each side; these are called 'No zones' and should be avoided.

question: Why must you use extra caution when driving at night?
options: a:Because drivers cannot see as well at night as during the day.,b:Because traffic moves faster at night.,c:Because there is more traffic at night.
note: From one half hour after sunset until one half hour before sunrise (or when you cannot see 500 feet), headlights must be used because visibility is reduced.

question: Is it ever acceptable to drive around or under a lowering or raising railroad crossing gate?
options: a:No — you must not drive around or under a gate that is moving.,b:Only if your vehicle can do so without damaging the gate.,c:Only when there are no visible trains.
note: Flashing lights, lowered gates, and bells mean stop; never drive around or under a gate while it is moving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If another driver is passing you, what should you do?
options: a:Check for oncoming traffic and adjust speed to let them complete the pass safely.,b:Signal to tell them when to pass.,c:Pull off the road.
note: When being passed, maintain speed or adjust so the passing vehicle can move back into your lane safely; do not accelerate to prevent the pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you use your turn signal?
options: a:All of the above — when changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, or pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.,b:Changing lanes.,c:Pulling into or out of a parking space.,d:Pulling into traffic from a parking area or alley.
note: You should always signal when making movements to the left or right, such as changing lanes, leaving or entering parking spaces, or pulling from an alley or curb.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Two solid white lines across a lane mark what area?
options: a:A crosswalk where pedestrians have the right-of-way.,b:A place where vehicles have right-of-way over pedestrians.,c:An area with no right-of-way rules.
note: Two solid white lines indicate a marked crosswalk; drivers must yield to pedestrians within the crosswalk.

question: Why must your vehicle be inspected at least once a year?
options: a:Only if it is older than five years old.,b:Unless it is a new vehicle.,c:To ensure it is safe to operate.
note: Annual vehicle inspections help ensure the vehicle is mechanically safe and in proper running condition.

question: When roads are slippery, what driving adjustment should you make?
options: a:Increase your following distance.,b:Drive as you would on dry roads.,c:Reduce use of turn signals.
note: On slippery surfaces give extra stopping distance because your vehicle will take longer to stop.

question: If you must slow down on a slippery road, what is the first action you should take?
options: a:Take your foot off the gas pedal to reduce speed.,b:Firmly apply your brakes immediately.,c:Apply your parking brake.
note: On slippery surfaces, first ease off the accelerator; if additional slowing is needed, apply brakes gently and steadily.

question: Compared to daytime driving, driving at night is:
options: a:No more or less dangerous.,b:Less dangerous.,c:More dangerous.
note: Night driving is more hazardous due to reduced visibility, glare from lights, and a higher likelihood of fatigued or impaired drivers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In which situations are you required to come to a stop?
options: a:At a stop sign, at a red light, and whenever a traffic officer orders you to stop.,b:Only at a stop sign.,c:Only when you see a flashing red light.
note: You must stop at stop signs, at a steady or flashing red light, and whenever a traffic officer directs you to stop.

question: How should you avoid collisions due to blind spots?
options: a:Quickly glance over your shoulder to check the blind spot before changing lanes.,b:Adjust rearview mirrors every few minutes.,c:Honk just before turning or changing lanes.
note: Turn your head and glance over your shoulder in the direction of the lane change; don't rely solely on mirrors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a flashing red traffic light mean?
options: a:The same thing as a stop sign.,b:The traffic signal is broken.,c:You do not have to come to a complete stop.
note: A flashing red light means stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when the way is clear.

question: Which statements about railroad crossings are true?
options: a:All of the following: It is against the law to go around lowered gates; you must stop when directed by a flagger; not all crossings have flashing lights and gates.,b:Only that all crossings have flashing red signals and gates.,c:You may drive around lowered gates if no train is visible.
note: You must obey flaggers and warning devices; not all crossings have gates or lights, and you must never go around a lowered gate.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A flashing red traffic signal at an intersection requires the same action as which device?
options: a:A stop sign.,b:A yield sign.,c:A slow sign.
note: A flashing red traffic signal means you must stop, just like at a stop sign, then proceed when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do before making a turn?
options: a:Increase your speed.,b:Use your signal.,c:Turn the wheel without signaling.
note: Activate your turn signal several seconds before making the turn so other road users know your intention.

question: Which action best describes a good defensive driver?
options: a:Travels at a constant speed at all times.,b:Looks out for the actions of other drivers and anticipates problems.,c:Drives slowly at all times.
note: A defensive driver anticipates others' actions, watches for hazards, and avoids assuming other drivers will behave perfectly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a work zone, what must you do?
options: a:Follow the directions given by the flagger.,b:Ignore the flagger and follow surrounding traffic.,c:Assume the flagger does not apply to you.
note: Obey flaggers in construction zones; failure to follow their directions is unsafe and can be illegal.

question: If you are taking a non-prescription (over-the-counter) drug, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Continue to drive regardless of any warning labels.,b:Drink alcohol instead.,c:Read the labels on the drug and heed any warnings about driving.
note: Many nonprescription medications impair driving; read labels and seek medical advice if unsure about driving while taking them.

question: Your blind spot is the area of the road that:
options: a:You see in your rearview mirror.,b:You cannot see without moving your head.,c:Is directly behind your vehicle.
note: Blind spots are areas, typically to the sides and just behind your vehicle, you cannot see without turning to look over your shoulder.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn at a green traffic light, you must:
options: a:Yield to oncoming traffic before completing the left turn.,b:Always have the right-of-way.,c:Always drive straight through the intersection.
note: When turning left on a green light, yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians; proceed only when it is safe to do so.

question: When backing a vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Turn your head and look through the rear window; do not rely solely on mirrors.,b:Rely only on your mirrors.,c:Open the door to check behind you.
note: Before and while backing, look over your shoulder through the rear window; children and small objects are hard to see using mirrors alone.

question: What is a reliable strategy to avoid driving while impaired after social drinking?
options: a:Arrange a ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.,b:Drink coffee before driving.,c:Take a cold shower to sober up quickly.
note: Plan a sober ride home; coffee or showers do not lower blood alcohol concentration.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, how should you turn the steering wheel?
options: a:In the direction you want the vehicle to go.,b:To keep the front wheels straight.,c:In the opposite direction of the skid.
note: Ease off the accelerator and steer in the direction you want the car to go; as it regains traction, straighten the wheel carefully.

question: When crossing railroad tracks, what should you do to be safe?
options: a:Cross especially quickly when a train is approaching.,b:Listen, look both ways, and then proceed if it is safe to do so.,c:Look both ways, but only when the red light is flashing.
note: Always look and listen for trains from both directions, obey active warnings, and only cross when you are certain it is safe.

question: After an accident, what is one of the first actions you should take?
options: a:Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes.,b:Turn off the ignition of any wrecked vehicles.,c:Stop your vehicle at or near the scene.
note: You must stop at or near the scene of a crash. If possible, move your vehicle out of traffic. Avoid standing in traffic lanes and turn off ignitions of wrecked vehicles when safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a right turn on a steady green light, what must you do?
options: a:Yield to pedestrians and other vehicles before turning.,b:Maintain your normal driving speed through the turn.,c:Stop and look only for police cars.
note: You may turn on green unless a sign prohibits it, but you must yield to pedestrians and other traffic in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it permissible to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Only when your lane is next to a broken yellow or white line and it is safe to pass.,b:In a curve or on a hill where visibility is limited.,c:By using the shoulder of the highway.
note: You may pass where pavement markings permit (e.g., a broken center line) and when you can see clearly ahead; never pass on hills, curves, or on the shoulder.

question: Which statement about seat belts and child restraints is true?
options: a:You should always make sure all your passengers are using a seat belt or child restraint.,b:You should never place an infant or small child in the front seat of a vehicle with airbags.,c:An airbag can be dangerous to an infant or small child, even in a low-speed collision.
note: Always ensure passengers are properly restrained; never place a rear-facing infant seat in a front seat equipped with an active passenger airbag.

question: What do your brake lights communicate to drivers behind you?
options: a:That you are slowing down or stopping.,b:That you are making a turn.,c:That your emergency brake is engaged.
note: Brake lights indicate to drivers behind you that you are slowing or stopping; keep them in working order.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving in the left lane and plan to move into the right lane, what should you do first?
options: a:Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your right shoulder for vehicles in the lane you intend to enter.,b:Check your mirrors, signal, and look over your left shoulder for traffic.,c:Check your mirrors, signal, and look over both shoulders.
note: When changing lanes, signal, check your mirrors, and look over your shoulder toward the lane you plan to enter to verify your blind spot is clear.

question: What is the effect of taking drugs with alcohol before driving?
options: a:It increases the risk of causing a crash by amplifying impairment.,b:It is no more dangerous than alcohol alone.,c:It reduces the alcohol's effects.
note: Combining drugs and alcohol can greatly increase impairment and the likelihood of a crash.

question: What is the purpose of regulatory signs?
options: a:To indicate actions drivers must or must not take in a designated area.,b:To mark scenic routes.,c:To mark areas of public recreation.
note: Regulatory signs (often white with black markings) tell drivers what they must or must not do, such as speed limits and turning restrictions.

question: If your power steering fails while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Work harder to steer, reduce your speed, safely pull off the road, and stop.,b:Turn on your hazard lights and immediately shut off the engine.,c:Honk continuously and continue driving to the nearest service station.
note: If power steering fails, control requires more effort; slow down and pull to a safe area to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your freeway exit, what is the correct action?
options: a:Pull onto the shoulder and back your car to the exit.,b:Go to the next exit.,c:Make a U-turn through the median.
note: If you miss your exit, continue to the next exit—do not stop, back up, or make unsafe maneuvers on the freeway.

question: When entering a street from a garage or alley, what must a driver do?
options: a:Yield to other drivers and pedestrians.,b:Assume you have the right-of-way.,c:Drive quickly to merge into traffic.
note: You must yield to vehicles and pedestrians on the public road when entering from a driveway, garage, or alley.

question: Why is a leaky exhaust system dangerous?
options: a:Because it can allow carbon monoxide to enter the passenger compartment and poison occupants.,b:Because it causes a loss of hearing.,c:Because it only increases pollution with no other effects.
note: A leaking exhaust can let carbon monoxide into the vehicle interior; repair exhaust leaks promptly.

question: What does a solid red arrow on a traffic signal mean?
options: a:The same as a circular red — stop and do not turn in the arrow’s direction.,b:You may turn with caution.,c:The arrow is not used as a traffic signal.
note: A solid red arrow means traffic in the indicated lane must stop and not turn in the arrow's direction until it changes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at an intersection at the same time without signs or signals, which vehicle has the right-of-way?
options: a:The vehicle approaching from the right.,b:The vehicle approaching from the left.,c:The vehicle whose driver sounds a horn first.
note: At intersections of two similar roads with no control device, yield to a vehicle approaching from your right.

question: Which factors greatly affect your ability to stop a vehicle?
options: a:Road surface and weather conditions (e.g., wet, icy, gravel),b:Only the signal lights at an intersection,c:The time of day you are driving.
note: Stopping distance is greatly influenced by pavement condition, weather, tire condition, and vehicle speed.

question: What color pavement markings separate traffic moving in opposite directions?
options: a:Yellow,b:White,c:Blue
note: Yellow center lines divide lanes of traffic traveling in opposite directions; white lines separate traffic moving the same way.

question: Before backing out of a driveway where children are playing, what should you do?
options: a:Get out and walk to the back of the car to be sure the way is clear.,b:Sound the horn to warn the children.,c:Start the car and back out slowly while watching your mirrors.
note: When children are nearby, exit the vehicle and check behind it rather than relying solely on mirrors or cameras.

question: When should you signal when passing another vehicle?
options: a:Just before changing lanes.,b:After changing lanes.,c:Early enough for other drivers to know your plans in advance.
note: Signal early enough—several seconds—so other road users understand your intended maneuver before you change lanes or pass.

question: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights of an approaching emergency vehicle, what must you do?
options: a:Motion for the emergency vehicle to pass you.,b:Stop your vehicle immediately and prevent them from passing.,c:Drive to the right side of the road and stop until it passes.
note: Yield the right-of-way: safely pull to the right and stop, or clear the intersection and then pull over to let the emergency vehicle pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you reach an intersection and need to turn but are in the wrong lane, what should you do?
options: a:Drive to the next intersection and make the turn from the correct lane.,b:Signal and make the turn from your current lane.,c:Quickly cut across traffic to complete the turn.
note: Never make last-minute lane changes or cuts across traffic. Proceed to the next intersection and turn from the proper lane.

question: On a vertically arranged traffic signal, what is the top-to-bottom order of lights?
options: a:Red, yellow, green.,b:Red, green, yellow.,c:Green, red, yellow.
note: On a vertical signal red is always on top and green on the bottom (horizontal signals have red on the left, green on the right).

question: If your vehicle's accelerator becomes stuck open, what action should you take?
options: a:Turn off the ignition carefully (avoiding locking the steering), apply the brakes, and move safely off the road.,b:Slam on the brakes immediately.,c:Turn on your four‑way flashers and continue driving.
note: If the accelerator sticks, take care to turn off the ignition only far enough to stop the engine (so the steering lock is not engaged), apply brakes, and steer safely off the roadway.

question: When is it permissible to cross double solid yellow lines?
options: a:To turn into or out of a driveway or to make a permitted left turn.,b:To pass a slow-moving truck.,c:To pass another car.
note: Double solid yellow lines generally prohibit passing; you may cross them to enter or exit a driveway or to make a permitted left turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which condition must be met before attempting to pass on a two-way, two-lane road?
options: a:All of the above — you must be able to see ahead, return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic, and have sufficient speed.,b:You must be able to return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.,c:Your vehicle must be capable of the speed necessary to complete the pass.,d:You must be able to clearly see the road ahead far enough to pass safely.
note: You may only pass on a two-way, two-lane road when you can see clearly ahead, can re-enter your lane before meeting oncoming traffic, and your vehicle can reach the speed needed to complete the pass safely.

question: What do crossbuck signs indicate?
options: a:A railroad crossing is ahead.,b:A school zone is ahead.,c:A no-passing zone.
note: Crossbuck signs mark railroad crossings and indicate you should yield to any approaching trains.

question: When a police officer stops you for a traffic violation or equipment inspection, what documents must you present?
options: a:Only proof of insurance.,b:License, vehicle registration, and proof of insurance.,c:Only the vehicle registration.
note: When stopped you must be able to produce your driver license, vehicle registration, and proof of insurance.

question: To prepare for hazards ahead, what driving technique should you use?
options: a:Drive with your left foot resting lightly on the brake pedal.,b:Continually scan the entire road and all roadsides.,c:Stare straight ahead at all times.
note: Search the roadway and roadside continually to identify problems early; do not stare just at the center of the road.

question: What should small-vehicle drivers be ready for when passing a large vehicle?
options: a:Wind gusts that can shift your vehicle's direction.,b:Loud engine noises only.,c:Extra air pollution but no steering effects.
note: Large vehicles create strong air currents that can push smaller vehicles; be prepared to correct steering.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning onto a street that has multiple lanes going your direction, into which lane should you turn?
options: a:Turn into the lane marked with an arrow.,b:Turn into the lane closest to the lane you are coming from.,c:Turn into the middle lane.
note: When turning onto a multilane street, enter the lane closest to the one you were in; avoid changing lanes during the turn.

question: What does a round traffic sign usually warn you about?
options: a:An upcoming railroad crossing.,b:A no-passing zone.,c:A school zone.
note: Round signs are used to warn drivers of an approaching railroad crossing; approach with caution.

question: Before passing another vehicle, what should you check?
options: a:Your mirrors and blind spots, and signal before changing lanes.,b:Honk to alert the driver to move over.,c:That you can re-enter within 10 feet of the passed vehicle.
note: Check mirrors and blind spots and signal before passing; re-enter when you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

question: On average, the human body eliminates alcohol at about what rate?
options: a:One standard alcoholic drink per hour.,b:Two alcoholic drinks per hour.,c:Three alcoholic drinks per hour.
note: Typically, the body processes about one standard drink per hour, though many factors affect impairment and metabolism rates.

question: Under what circumstances may you drive around railroad crossing gates?
options: a:Under no circumstances.,b:When the lights have stopped flashing and the train is gone.,c:If the train has just passed and the gate is still lowering.
note: You must not go around lowered or lowering gates; wait until the lights and bells stop and the gates are fully raised.

question: Which statement about sudden weather changes is correct?
options: a:All of the following are true: adjust your driving for sudden weather changes, slow down in rain or fog, and be mindful of vehicles behind you.,b:Only slow down in rain and fog.,c:Only be concerned about vehicles ahead of you.
note: When weather changes suddenly you must change your driving — slow down in rain or fog and watch for vehicles behind you.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light indicate?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Stop and wait for a green light.,c:Speed up to clear the intersection.
note: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed carefully through the intersection.

question: When may you drive across a dashed white line?
options: a:When it is safe to change lanes.,b:Only during daylight hours.,c:At any time even if unsafe.
note: Dashed white lines mean lanes travel in the same direction and you may cross them to pass or change lanes when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes on a highway, you should:
options: a:All of the above — signal, check mirrors, and check your blind spot.,b:Signal a lane change.,c:Check your rearview and outside mirrors.,d:Check your blind spot by glancing over your shoulder.
note: Before changing lanes signal well in advance, check your mirrors, and glance over your shoulder to verify the blind spot is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A sign reading 'Reduced speed, 35 mph' indicates what?
options: a:The new 35 mph speed limit begins at this sign.,b:The new 35 mph speed limit begins at the next posted speed limit sign.,c:That you have plenty of time to slow before the reduced zone.
note: A posted reduced-speed sign indicates the new speed limit begins at that sign and you must slow accordingly.

question: Which of these is not a safe action when passing another road user?
options: a:Signaling to let other drivers know you will change lanes.,b:Allowing a bicyclist extra room when passing them on the roadway.,c:Leaving less than four feet of space between your vehicle and the vehicle you are overtaking.
note: When passing, always leave at least four feet of space, especially when passing bicycles; signal and be cautious.

question: Is it legal to drink alcoholic beverages in a vehicle on a public road?
options: a:No — consuming or possessing open alcohol on public roads is illegal.,b:Yes if you are a passenger in the back seat.,c:Yes if you are in the bed of a pickup truck.
note: It is illegal to consume or possess open alcoholic beverages on public roads; open containers in areas accessible to driver or passengers are prohibited.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following statements about speed is true?
options: a:Speeding is not dangerous if you are a skilled driver.,b:Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.,c:Speeding can kill.
note: Higher speeds increase crash severity and the chance of death; speeding is deadly even for skilled drivers.

question: How is distracted driving best described?
options: a:Extremely risky behavior that endangers everyone on the road.,b:A rare occurrence.,c:Nothing to be concerned about.
note: Distracted driving dramatically increases the risk of a crash by diverting attention from driving tasks.

question: Which practices can help reduce road rage and aggressive driving?
options: a:Obeying posted speed limits.,b:Allowing extra travel time.,c:Using proper turn signals.
note: Allowing extra time, obeying speed limits, and signaling properly all reduce stress and lower the chance of road rage.

question: If you are in the right lane and want to move into the left lane on a multilane highway, what should you do?
options: a:Look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot and signal before changing lanes.,b:Just check your rearview mirror and move over slowly.,c:Turn on your hazard lights and move left.
note: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and look over your shoulder toward the lane you intend to enter to check the blind spot; always signal.

question: Which of these items can be a distraction while driving?
options: a:CD players, iPods, cell phones, and GPS devices.,b:Food and beverages.,c:Pets moving around inside the vehicle.
note: Portable electronics, eating, and pets can all divert your eyes and attention from driving; avoid distractions.

question: What should be your first response to reduced visibility?
options: a:Reduce your speed.,b:Turn on windshield wipers only.,c:Turn on interior lights.
note: Your first response to decreased visibility or hazardous conditions should be to slow down.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If the line dividing your lane from the lane you wish to enter is what type of line may you pass?
options: a:Broken white.,b:Double solid yellow.,c:Solid yellow.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes going the same direction and may be crossed to change lanes or pass when safe.

question: Which of the following can impair your ability to drive?
options: a:All of the following: alcohol, medications, and lack of sleep.,b:Only alcohol.,c:Only lack of sleep.
note: Alcohol, legal and illegal drugs, and drowsiness can each reduce a driver’s ability to operate a vehicle safely.

question: How should you behave when you see a blind pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog?
options: a:Take the right-of-way.,b:Slow down and be prepared to stop.,c:Proceed normally at the same speed.
note: Yield to blind pedestrians, slow down, and be prepared to stop to avoid endangering them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following locations is passing prohibited?
options: a:On hills and curves.,b:At all times on two-lane roads.,c:Only when following large trucks.
note: Passing is unlawful and unsafe on hills, curves, at intersections, and at railroad crossings because visibility is limited.

question: When an emergency vehicle is displaying flashing red or blue lights and approaching, what must you do?
options: a:Continue driving but try to stay out of its way.,b:See if you can reach your destination before it catches up to you.,c:Pull over to the side of the road and come to a complete stop.
note: Yield to all emergency vehicles using lights or sirens: pull to the right edge of the road and stop until they have passed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before making a left turn, it is important to:
options: a:Yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.,b:Sound your horn to warn others.,c:Swing to the right side of your lane before turning.
note: When turning left you must yield the right-of-way to oncoming traffic and pedestrians; proceed only when the way is clear.

question: Which of the following is NOT a factor in determining stopping distance?
options: a:Steering ability,b:Braking distance,c:Reaction distance
note: Stopping distance depends on perception time, reaction distance, and braking distance; steering ability is not a primary factor in the calculation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a stop sign in a line of vehicles, if there is no cross traffic after vehicles ahead have cleared, what must you do?
options: a:Stop again at the stop sign or stop line before proceeding.,b:Proceed without stopping since others already did.,c:Slowly roll past the stop sign without stopping.
note: You must come to a full stop at the stop sign each time and yield to traffic before proceeding; do not roll through.

question: If you are driving in another vehicle's blind spot, what is the correct action?
options: a:Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.,b:Maintain your position and speed.,c:Stay in the blind spot to prevent lane changes.
note: Do not remain in another vehicle's blind spot; adjust your position so the other driver can see you clearly.

question: What most often causes motor vehicle crashes?
options: a:Poor road conditions.,b:Actions or errors on the part of the driver.,c:Large trucks.
note: Most crashes are caused by driver actions or errors; safe driving practices and attention reduce crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing for a right turn, where should your vehicle be positioned?
options: a:As close to the right side of the road as possible.,b:Near the center of the street.,c:Close to the left side of the street.
note: Position your vehicle as far right as practicable before making a right turn; do not cut across lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it permissible to stop in a travel lane to look up an address or drop off passengers?
options: a:No — you should not stop in a travel lane; pull off the road to a safe place.,b:Yes — you may stop to drop off passengers.,c:Yes — you may stop to look up an address.
note: You should not stop in a travel lane; continue to a safe area to pull off the roadway if you must stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A steady red traffic signal requires you to:
options: a:Stop before entering any crosswalk.,b:Stop at the stop line.,c:Stop before entering the intersection.
note: At a red light you must stop at the marked stop line, and if none, before entering any crosswalk or the intersection.

question: Signs that warn you of hazardous conditions are called:
options: a:Warning signs.,b:Regulatory signs.,c:Information signs.
note: Warning signs alert drivers to possible hazards or changes in roadway conditions and should be obeyed to avoid accidents.

question: Which factor does vehicle stopping distance not depend on?
options: a:The condition of your vehicle's brakes.,b:Your own reaction time.,c:The time of day.
note: Stopping distance depends on reaction time, vehicle weight, brakes, tire condition, roadway, and speed; time of day itself is not a direct factor.

question: When approaching a flashing red traffic light, drivers should:
options: a:Come to a complete stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and then proceed when safe.,b:Drive through the intersection if there is no crossing traffic.,c:Continue driving because they have the right-of-way.
note: A flashing red traffic light should be treated like a stop sign: stop completely, yield, then proceed when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection, when must you stop for a traffic signal?
options: a:For a steady yellow light.,b:For a flashing red light.,c:For a yellow arrow.
note: A flashing red traffic signal means the same as a stop sign: come to a complete stop, yield, and proceed only when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving so slowly that traffic is backing up behind you on a two-lane, two-way road, what must you do?
options: a:Decrease your speed further.,b:Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.,c:Not let the other cars pass your vehicle.
note: If you are impeding traffic by driving too slowly, you must pull off when safe and allow others to pass.

question: To relieve fatigue on a long trip, what is a good practice?
options: a:Stop and rest every two hours.,b:Drive with one eye open at a time.,c:Do arm exercises every hour.
note: Take regular breaks—about every two hours—rest or nap if drowsy, and avoid continuing to drive while fatigued.

question: Which practice helps prevent crashes by making your intentions clear to others?
options: a:Communicate with other road users by signaling and using appropriate warnings.,b:Ignore other drivers on the road.,c:Drive only on side streets to avoid traffic.
note: Use signals, horn, and lights as appropriate to communicate your actions to motorists, bicyclists, and pedestrians.

question: Does the type of alcoholic beverage change how alcohol affects your judgment and reflexes?
options: a:No — any alcoholic beverage can impair reflexes and judgment depending on amount.,b:Yes — beer has much less effect than wine.,c:Yes — hard ciders affect you most.
note: All alcoholic drinks affect your bloodstream similarly; impairment depends on amount consumed, not type of beverage.

question: Which factors affect braking distance?
options: a:Vehicle speed, condition of brakes and tires, and pavement condition.,b:Color of the vehicle.,c:The radio volume.
note: Braking distance depends on speed, brake/tire condition, and road surface; these determine how long it takes to stop.

question: How can you avoid the risks of alcohol-related crashes?
options: a:Decide before you start drinking that you will not drive.,b:Say 'No thanks, I'm driving' only when offered a drink.,c:Drink slowly to avoid impairment.
note: The safest option is to plan ahead and arrange not to drive before drinking; alcohol impairs judgement and decision-making.

question: A person walking with a white cane or guide dog is most likely to be:
options: a:A person who is blind or visually impaired.,b:Participating in a traffic study.,c:Deaf.
note: Drivers must always yield the right-of-way to pedestrians who are blind and using a white cane or guide dog.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on a freeway, what is the proper action?
options: a:Stop and back up.,b:Continue driving until the next exit, turn, or safe place to change direction.,c:Make the turn quickly from your lane of travel.
note: Do not back up or make sudden turns; proceed to the next exit or other safe location to leave the freeway and turn around.

question: What are the usual colors for warning signs about upcoming hazards?
options: a:Black symbols or letters on a yellow background.,b:White on blue.,c:Black on white.
note: Warning signs typically use black symbols or text on a yellow background; work zone warnings are orange with black.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you respond to a flashing yellow traffic light?
options: a:Turn on your headlights.,b:Come to a complete stop.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light warns of a hazard: reduce speed and proceed carefully through the area.

question: At dusk or on overcast days, what should you do regarding vehicle lighting?
options: a:Turn on your headlights (low beam) so others can see you.,b:Drive using only your parking lights.,c:Not turn on any lights.
note: At dusk or overcast conditions you must turn on headlights; use low beams within 1,000 feet of oncoming vehicles and 500 feet when following.

question: Which general rule should you follow about passing other vehicles?
options: a:Drive with traffic flow and pass only when necessary.,b:Pass on the right whenever possible.,c:Try to get to the front of slow traffic to see better.
note: Passing increases collision risk; stay with the flow of traffic within speed limits and pass only when needed.

question: When should you use your turn signal?
options: a:Pulling into traffic from an alley or parking area.,b:Changing lanes.,c:Pulling into or out of a parking space.
note: Always signal when changing lanes, entering traffic from an alley or parking area, or pulling into/out of a parking space to alert others.

question: What does a regulatory sign with a red circle and a slash through a symbol indicate?
options: a:That drivers should come to a complete stop.,b:That some drivers should yield to other drivers.,c:That the action shown is forbidden.
note: A red circle with a slash over a black symbol indicates that the specified action (such as turning or U-turns) is prohibited.

question: Who should wear seat belts to be most effective?
options: a:All occupants of a vehicle.,b:The driver only.,c:Only passengers on long trips.
note: Seat belts are most effective when everyone in the vehicle is properly buckled; unbelted occupants become hazards in crashes.

question: On a two-lane street being followed by a fire engine that is NOT using lights or siren, you should:
options: a:Continue to drive in a normal manner.,b:Stop as quickly as you can.,c:Speed up to get out of its way.
note: If an emergency vehicle behind you is not using siren or flashing lights, you do not need to clear the way; continue driving normally.

question: When is it appropriate to use your horn?
options: a:To alert others if you lose control or to avoid a collision.,b:Only when passing another car.,c:To express frustration at other drivers.
note: Use your horn to warn others of danger, such as when you lose control; avoid using it to express anger.

question: When a school bus is stopped with red lights flashing, what must you do?
options: a:Stop — it is illegal to pass the bus.,b:Proceed slowly if you do not see children.,c:Pass if the bus is on the opposite side of a divided highway only.
note: You must stop for a stopped school bus with red lights flashing; on a divided highway with a physical separation, traffic on the other side may continue.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How would you best define a speed limit?
options: a:The maximum or minimum legal speed you may travel under ideal conditions.,b:The recommended safe speed under all conditions.,c:The suggested speed only for heavy vehicles.
note: A speed limit is the maximum (or minimum, where posted) legal speed under ideal conditions; adjust your speed for road or weather conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How close to the right edge of the road should your vehicle be when preparing to make a right turn?
options: a:About three feet from the right side of the road.,b:About one foot from the right side of the road.,c:About five feet from the right side of the road.
note: When preparing to turn right, position your vehicle about three feet from the right edge of the roadway.

question: Which statement best describes a drowsy driver?
options: a:Drowsy drivers can perform so poorly that their driving may resemble that of a drunk driver.,b:Opening a window and turning up the radio will keep them alert.,c:Drinking strong coffee is an effective long-term solution.
note: Drowsiness impairs driving and can mimic intoxication; simple measures like windows or radio usually do not restore full alertness.

question: If convicted of passing a stopped school bus with its red warning lights activated, you will:
options: a:Be required to pay a substantial fine and have five points added to your driving record.,b:Receive two points on your license.,c:Receive only a written warning.
note: In Vermont, failing to stop for a stopped school bus displaying red lights is punishable by a substantial fine and the assessment of five points on your driving record.

question: What can happen if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medicine?
options: a:The combination can multiply the impairing effects of both the alcohol and the medicine.,b:The medicine will cancel the alcohol's effects.,c:Alcohol helps the medicine work faster.
note: Combining alcohol with medications can amplify impairment and lead to unpredictable, dangerous effects.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What do speed limit signs indicate?
options: a:The maximum or minimum speed that is legally allowed to be driven.,b:Potential driving speeds for the area,c:The speed drivers should drive in heavy traffic.
note: Speed limit signs set the legal maximum (and sometimes minimum) under ideal conditions; reduce speed when conditions require.

question: After a stopped school bus has finished unloading children, what should you do?
options: a:Watch for children walking along the roadside and proceed cautiously.,b:Accelerate quickly to clear the bus area.,c:Proceed only after the bus driver waves at you.
note: After a school bus stops and children disembark, be alert for children near the roadway and proceed with caution when safe.

question: Which recommendation does NOT help safe night driving?
options: a:Carrying a flashlight in your vehicle.,b:Being aware that dark-tinted windows reduce nighttime visibility.,c:Keeping your windshield dirty so glare is reduced.
note: Keep your windshield clean, be mindful that tint reduces night visibility, and carry a flashlight. A dirty windshield increases glare and reduces visibility.

question: On a road without sidewalks, which way should a pedestrian walk?
options: a:Facing oncoming traffic (on the left side of the road).,b:With the flow of traffic (on the right side).,c:On the side with the lightest traffic.
note: Pedestrians should walk facing traffic so they can see oncoming vehicles and react accordingly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, what is usually the best approach?
options: a:Use the on-ramp to accelerate to the speed of freeway traffic and merge when safe.,b:Proceed slowly while waiting for a large gap.,c:Turn on your hazard lights while merging.
note: Use the acceleration lane to match the speed of freeway traffic so you can merge smoothly; entering traffic must yield to vehicles on the freeway.

question: What do double solid yellow lines down the middle of the road mean?
options: a:Passing is not allowed from either direction.,b:Indication of a railroad crossing ahead.,c:Only pedestrians may cross here.
note: Double solid yellow lines indicate no passing in either direction except for permitted left turns or when safe passing of non-motorized users is allowed.

question: An octagonal traffic sign always means:
options: a:A stop sign.,b:A speed limit sign.,c:A hospital sign.
note: The eight-sided (octagonal) sign always indicates a stop sign; come to a complete stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a busy freeway, what should you do to merge safely?
options: a:Use the acceleration lane to adjust your speed to match freeway traffic.,b:Yield to freeway traffic without attempting to match speed.,c:Enter the freeway slowly and then accelerate after merging.
note: Use the entrance ramp to accelerate to the speed of freeway traffic, check mirrors and blind spots, and yield to vehicles already on the freeway before merging.

question: How must you respond when you approach a railroad crossing with flashing warning signals?
options: a:Stop and look for a train, obeying the crossing warnings.,b:Slow down and look for a train but continue if the way looks clear.,c:Look for a train, then speed up to cross quickly.
note: When railroad signals are flashing or gates are down you must stop; stop no closer than 15 feet from the nearest rail when warning signals are active.

question: When you pass a horse and rider on the road, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down, move over, and avoid using your horn so you do not startle the horse.,b:Sound your horn to warn the rider of your approach.,c:Pass quickly to reduce time near the horse.
note: Horses can be easily frightened; slow down, give them space, and avoid horn use or sudden acceleration.

question: How should you adjust your following distance when driving on slippery roads?
options: a:Increase your following distance and reduce speed.,b:Use cruise control to maintain a steady distance.,c:Reduce your following distance to improve traffic flow.
note: On slippery roads, increase following distance, slow down, and avoid cruise control to preserve vehicle control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it legal to pass by crossing a double solid yellow centerline?
options: a:Yes.,b:No.,c:If there is no oncoming traffic.
note: Double solid yellow lines prohibit passing; you may only cross such lines to turn into a driveway or make a legal left turn.

question: What is the effect of eating or drinking while driving?
options: a:Are better drivers because they are not hungry.,b:Make no driving errors.,c:Are more likely to make driving errors because of the distraction.
note: Eating, drinking, or handling items while driving diverts hands and eyes from driving, increasing the chance of errors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If stopped by a police officer, what is the recommended behavior?
options: a:Get your paperwork ready before the officer reaches your car.,b:Unbuckle your seat belt and lower your window.,c:Stay in your vehicle with your hands visible on the steering wheel and wait for the officer to approach.
note: Remain in the vehicle with hands visible, avoid sudden movements, and wait for the officer to request your license and registration.

question: For a driver age 21 or older, at what minimum BAC is it illegal to operate a motor vehicle?
options: a:0.08 percent.,b:0.05 percent.,c:0.02 percent.
note: For those 21 and older it is illegal to drive with a BAC of 0.08% or higher.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to make a left turn, what should drivers do?
options: a:Move into the left lane and signal, watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians.,b:Slow down gradually while checking their rearview mirror only.,c:Watch for oncoming vehicles and pedestrians and yield when necessary.
note: Signal several seconds in advance, check mirrors, move into the correct lane as appropriate, yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, and turn when clear.

question: Drivers should know that large trucks:
options: a:Have large blind spots and require more room to maneuver and stop.,b:Can stop more quickly than passenger vehicles.,c:Do not need extra room to maneuver compared with passenger cars.
note: Large trucks have significant blind spots to the front, sides, and rear and need more space to maneuver and stop than passenger vehicles.

question: What should you do after rain begins while driving?
options: a:Slow down and turn on your headlights so others can see you.,b:Increase your speed to reduce time in the rain.,c:Drive at the posted maximum speed.
note: When rain reduces visibility slow down and use headlights; if visibility is severely reduced, pull off safely and stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are already within an intersection and the light turns yellow, when may you continue through?
options: a:If you are turning right.,b:If there is an emergency vehicle crossing your lane.,c:If there are pedestrians crossing.
note: If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, proceed through carefully to clear the intersection; otherwise prepare to stop when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a yield sign require you to do?
options: a:Yield to traffic in the roadway you are entering or to traffic already in the intersection.,b:Always stop before entering the intersection.,c:Yield only to traffic on the right.
note: A yield sign means slow down, be prepared to stop, and give the right-of-way to traffic and pedestrians in the intersection or roadway you are entering.

question: Why should drivers be especially alert for motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?
options: a:Because they are smaller and more difficult to see in traffic.,b:Because they always have different traffic laws.,c:Because they always have the right-of-way.
note: Smaller road users are harder to detect; pay extra attention because they may move unpredictably and have less visibility.

question: When should you use high-beam headlights at night?
options: a:When driving in open country where there are few other vehicles.,b:When meeting an oncoming vehicle.,c:When you are following another vehicle closely.
note: Use high beams on open roads with few cars present; dim them when approaching or following other vehicles.

question: If an approaching driver fails to dim high-beam headlights, where should you look?
options: a:Toward the right side of the road.,b:At the wheels of the approaching vehicle.,c:Toward the left side of the road.
note: Glance toward the right edge of the road to avoid the glare from oncoming high beams while maintaining your lane position.

question: When you hear the siren of a fire engine behind you, what must you do?
options: a:Drive with your flashers on.,b:Pull over to the side of the road and stop.,c:Slow down until it passes you.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with a siren, pull to the curb or right side of the road and stop to allow it to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct sequence of actions when changing lanes?
options: a:Signal, check mirrors, glance over your shoulder to check the blind spot, then change lanes.,b:Signal and change immediately after checking mirrors.,c:Check mirrors, then signal and change lanes without checking the blind spot.
note: Before changing lanes, signal, check your rearview and side mirrors, and look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to verify your blind spot is clear.

question: What is the effect of combining alcohol with drugs?
options: a:It can increase the effects of both the alcohol and the drugs.,b:It decreases the effects of both.,c:It helps cure your illness.
note: Alcohol and drugs can interact to increase impairment and make driving even more dangerous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: From a center left-turn lane, which maneuvers are permitted?
options: a:Making left turns from either direction into and out of the lane.,b:Using the lane to pass slow-moving traffic.,c:Driving straight through the intersection.
note: Center turn lanes are reserved for left turns from either direction; they are not for passing or through traffic.

question: You arrive at an intersection with a flashing red light. What must you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop and proceed when safe.,b:Slow down and yield to traffic then go.,c:Wait for a flashing green light.
note: A flashing red signal means stop completely; proceed only when the way is clear.

question: How can you reduce your risk of hydroplaning?
options: a:Drive more slowly in wet conditions.,b:Drive faster to get through water quickly.,c:Drive through deep water to clear tires.
note: Hydroplaning risk decreases when you reduce speed in wet conditions so tires can maintain contact with the road.

question: Which substances may impair your ability to drive and lead to DUII?
options: a:Alcohol, illegal drugs, inhalants, and certain prescription or over-the-counter medicines.,b:Only beer and wine.,c:Only illicit hard drugs.
note: A wide range of substances including alcohol, illegal drugs, inhalants, and many legal medications can impair driving and lead to DUII.

question: Which of these actions reduces your risk of hydroplaning on wet roads?
options: a:Do all of the following — slow down, keep tires properly inflated, and replace tires with bad tread.,b:Only maintain correct tire pressure.,c:Only replace tires with bad tread.
note: Hydroplaning risk is reduced by slowing down on wet roads, maintaining proper tire pressure, and replacing tires with worn tread.

question: In what ways can alcoholic beverages affect your driving?
options: a:It gives you a feeling of false confidence.,b:It impairs your thinking ability.,c:It slows your reaction time.
note: Alcohol impairs judgment, coordination, and reaction time and may give a false sense of confidence; all reduce driving ability.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If entering the roadway from a driveway or private road, what should you do?
options: a:Yield to drivers already on the public road.,b:Assume you have the right-of-way.,c:Force your way into traffic if necessary.
note: When entering public traffic, yield to vehicles already on the road and merge safely.

question: What factors determine how much space you need to cross traffic safely?
options: a:Road conditions, weather conditions, and oncoming traffic.,b:Whether a stop sign is present.,c:The use of your turn signal.
note: The space needed to cross traffic safely depends on road and weather conditions and the speed and distance of oncoming vehicles.

question: At night, which road users are hardest to see?
options: a:Pedestrians.,b:Road signs.,c:Other motorists.
note: Pedestrians are the hardest to see at night compared to signs or other roadside objects; use caution and proper lighting.

question: How should you prepare when driving to an unfamiliar area?
options: a:Plan your trip in advance and check maps or directions before you go.,b:Depend solely on road signs as you drive.,c:Drive without a clear idea of your destination.
note: Plan routes ahead of time so you are not distracted or uncertain while driving in unfamiliar areas.

question: What is the primary cause of hydroplaning?
options: a:Driving too fast on a wet surface so the tires cannot clear water effectively.,b:Sudden stops alone.,c:Only worn brakes.
note: Hydroplaning occurs when tires cannot displace water at higher speeds and the vehicle rides on a film of water.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you pass your exit while on the interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.,b:Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.,c:Continue driving and use the next exit.
note: Do not stop or back up on the highway; proceed to the next exit and safely return to your intended exit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do when turning or changing lanes?
options: a:Always signal your intention, even if no visible traffic is present.,b:Only signal if other vehicles are visible.,c:Only signal at night.
note: Always use turn signals when changing lanes or turning so other road users know your intentions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see a merging traffic sign on a multilane roadway, what should you do?
options: a:Always remain at your present speed.,b:Move over one lane when safe to make room for entering vehicles.,c:Honk at incoming traffic to warn them.
note: On multi-lane roads make room for entering traffic by moving over a lane when it is safe to do so.

question: Why must other drivers allow extra room around heavy trucks?
options: a:The decreased noise of larger vehicles.,b:The increased stopping distance required by large vehicles.,c:The decreased stopping distance required by large vehicles.
note: Large trucks need much more distance to stop; allow space and remain where the truck driver can see you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you make a right turn at a solid red light?
options: a:After coming to a complete stop, yielding to pedestrians and vehicles, unless a sign prohibits the turn.,b:Any time traffic is light.,c:Only when a police officer signals you to turn.
note: Unless posted otherwise, you may turn right on red after a full stop and after yielding to pedestrians and other traffic.

question: What will help someone overcome the effects of alcoholic drinks?
options: a:Only the passage of time.,b:Drinking tomato juice and lime.,c:Drinking hot coffee or getting fresh air.
note: Nothing will remove alcohol effects quickly; only time allows the body to eliminate alcohol.

question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, what is the advisable response?
options: a:Stay calm and move out of the aggressive driver's way.,b:Flash lights and yell to teach them a lesson.,c:Immediately call the aggressive driver names while driving.
note: Remain calm, avoid escalation, and safely move away from the aggressive driver to reduce risk.

question: If you leave your vehicle unattended, what actions are required?
options: a:Turn off the engine only.,b:Lock the ignition and remove the key, stop the engine, and set the parking brake.,c:Set the parking brake only.
note: When leaving your vehicle, stop the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake to secure the vehicle.

question: How should you behave when you see a school crossing sign?
options: a:Watch carefully for children and be prepared to stop.,b:Always come to a stop whether a sign or not.,c:Always sound your horn to warn children.
note: Be alert to pedestrians (especially children) at school crossings and be ready to stop when necessary.

question: What does a single broken white line between lanes mean?
options: a:Lanes are moving in the same direction and you may pass when it is safe to do so.,b:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and you may pass when safe.,c:Lanes are moving in the same direction and passing is prohibited.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction; drivers next to the line may pass when it is safe.

question: How should you check blind spots before changing lanes?
options: a:Turn your head and look over your shoulder to verify the blind spot.,b:Rely only on the inside rearview mirror.,c:Use only the outside mirror on the side you intend to move toward.
note: Always turn your head to glance over your shoulder in the direction you intend to move to ensure your blind spot is clear.

question: When driving in regular traffic, what speed strategy is generally safest?
options: a:Drive with the flow of traffic while staying within the posted speed limit.,b:Drive faster than the surrounding traffic to get through quickly.,c:Drive significantly slower than other vehicles to be cautious.
note: Crashes often occur when drivers go much faster or slower than the flow; aim to drive with the traffic flow within legal limits.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering heavy interstate traffic from an entrance ramp, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Drivers already on the interstate.,b:The entering driver has the right-of-way.,c:Interstate drivers must wave entering drivers into traffic.
note: Drivers already on the interstate have the right-of-way; entering traffic must yield and merge when safe.

question: If it starts to sleet or snow while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Keep windshield and mirrors clear and increase following distance.,b:Speed up to get out of the area quickly.,c:Ignore other vehicles nearby.
note: Keep visibility clear and allow extra stopping distance as slippery surfaces increase stopping distances.

question: Which traffic signal requires you to come to a complete stop, yield to cross traffic and pedestrians, and then proceed when clear?
options: a:Flashing red light.,b:Solid green light.,c:Flashing yellow light.
note: A flashing red light must be treated like a stop sign: stop completely, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then continue when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you pull over and allow an emergency vehicle with lights and siren to pass?
options: a:Regardless of the emergency vehicle's direction of travel.,b:Only if it is following you.,c:Only if it is approaching from the opposite direction.
note: You must pull over to the right and stop for emergency vehicles with flashing lights or sirens, no matter which direction they are coming from.

question: When must you stop for a school bus?
options: a:When it approaches you, even if its lights are not flashing.,b:That is parked on the shoulder of the road with no one in it.,c:If you are driving on a two-lane highway and its red lights are flashing.
note: You must stop for a stopped school bus with flashing red lights (and extended stop arm) on two-lane roads; vehicles in both directions must stop.

question: Why must you be cautious when passing a bicyclist?
options: a:Oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass, and the cyclist may swerve to avoid hazards.,b:Bicyclists always have the right-of-way and you must stop.,c:Because bicycles are always traveling faster than cars.
note: Bicyclists can swerve to avoid debris or obstacles; be sure you have clearance and that oncoming traffic sees you when passing.

question: What do pennant-shaped traffic signs indicate?
options: a:No passing zones.,b:School zones.,c:Speed limits.
note: Pennant-shaped signs placed on the left side of the road indicate a no passing zone.

question: What is a 'No zone' with respect to large vehicles?
options: a:The blind spot area around a truck or large vehicle.,b:A one-way traffic area.,c:A designated no-passing zone.
note: 'No zones' are large blind spots around trucks where smaller vehicles should avoid lingering to remain visible to the truck driver.

question: Where is it best to keep a space cushion around your vehicle?
options: a:On all sides of your vehicle.,b:Only on the left and right sides of your vehicle.,c:Only behind your vehicle.
note: Maintain space on all sides—front, back, and both sides—so you have time and room to react to hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, which way should you turn your wheels?
options: a:Turn your wheels to the right so the vehicle will roll away from traffic if it moves.,b:Turn your wheels to the left.,c:Keep your wheels straight ahead.
note: When parked facing downhill, turn your wheels toward the curb (to the right) so the vehicle will roll into the curb rather than into traffic if it moves.

question: When must a driver change lanes to create space for a stopped emergency or maintenance vehicle?
options: a:When approaching a stopped maintenance vehicle using flashing amber lights.,b:When approaching a stopped police vehicle using flashing blue lights.,c:When approaching a stopped vehicle using flashing blue, red, or amber lights.
note: You must move over a lane to provide space for stopped police (blue), emergency (red), or maintenance/roadside assistance (amber) vehicles when safe to do so.

question: If an oncoming vehicle is heading into your lane, what is the recommended immediate action?
options: a:Blow your horn, steer to the right, and brake to avoid a head-on collision.,b:Blow your horn, steer left, and accelerate.,c:Brake lightly and hold your lane.
note: Honk to attract attention, steer right to avoid the oncoming vehicle, and brake firmly if needed; do not swerve left into oncoming traffic.

question: If you borrow an unfamiliar vehicle, what should you do before driving it?
options: a:Assume all vehicles are identical and start driving.,b:Take a few minutes to locate and learn how to operate the controls and correct any obvious defects before driving.,c:Disregard any defects to avoid embarrassing the owner.
note: Before driving an unfamiliar vehicle, familiarize yourself with turn signals, lights, wipers, brakes, gear selector, horn, and correct any safety defects.

question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
options: a:Human error.,b:Bad weather.,c:New drivers.
note: Most crashes result from human error — failing to see other vehicles, misjudging situations, or making unexpected maneuvers.

question: Lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions are divided by what color lines?
options: a:Yellow lines.,b:White lines.,c:Red lines.
note: Yellow pavement markings separate opposing traffic directions; white marks lanes moving the same direction.

question: When confronted with an oncoming car on your left and a bicyclist on your right, how should you proceed?
options: a:Split the difference and squeeze between them.,b:Pull onto the shoulder.,c:Let the oncoming car pass first, then pass the bicyclist when it is safe.
note: Avoid trying to handle two hazards at once: allow the oncoming car to pass, then give the bicyclist sufficient space before passing.

question: How can you ensure your physical condition won’t impair your driving?
options: a:Know how any medicine affects your driving and drive within your limitations.,b:Only drive when you feel strong.,c:Ignore minor health warnings when driving.
note: Be aware of medications' effects, keep fit, have regular checkups, and only drive if it’s safe given your physical condition.

question: Which of the following about winter driving is NOT true?
options: a:Using cruise control in winter weather is safe.,b:Winter is the most difficult driving season.,c:Check antifreeze and washer fluid levels before winter driving.
note: Do not use cruise control in snowy, icy, or similar hazardous conditions; winter requires extra caution and vehicle checks.

question: Which is the safest way to drive through a curve?
options: a:Slow down as you enter the curve and gradually speed up as you exit.,b:Maintain a constant speed throughout no matter the conditions.,c:Speed up as you enter and slow down as you exit.
note: Reduce speed before entering a curve and accelerate gently as you exit to maintain control.

question: When does your vehicle's stopping distance increase?
options: a:On wet or icy roads.,b:On paved highways in good weather.,c:Only when driving at night.
note: Stopping distance increases greatly on slippery surfaces like wet or icy roads and on loose gravel.

question: Lack of sleep affects driving ability similarly to what?
options: a:The effects of alcohol.,b:The effects of amphetamines.,c:The effects of being angry.
note: Fatigue impairs driving in a way comparable to alcohol; long wakefulness can equate to significant BAC impairment.

question: Which practice helps prevent drowsiness on long trips?
options: a:Stopping regularly to rest and stretch.,b:Keeping the radio on loud.,c:Reducing your speed significantly.
note: Schedule regular stops to rest and stretch. Short breaks help you stay alert on long drives.

question: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down and very carefully steer back onto the pavement.,b:Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the pavement.,c:Stop your car on the edge of the road.
note: If your wheels drop onto a low shoulder, reduce speed without braking, then carefully steer back onto the pavement when safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a turn, how should you adjust your speed?
options: a:Maintain your speed.,b:Vary your speed so you reduce it to a safe turning pace.,c:Increase your speed.
note: Reduce your speed to a level that allows you to remain in control, stay in your lane, and react to unexpected situations while turning.

question: Which statement about work zones is correct?
options: a:Work zones may be stationary or moving and are marked with orange signs.,b:They are marked with black and white signs only.,c:Drivers are not required to slow down in work zones.
note: Work zones may be moving or stationary and are marked with orange signs; slow down and pay extra attention.

question: Two solid yellow lines on the pavement indicate what?
options: a:Passing is not permitted.,b:Passing is allowed from both directions.,c:You may pass when at the top of a hill.
note: Two solid yellow center lines mean passing is prohibited for traffic in both directions.

question: When changing lanes, what are important actions to take?
options: a:Make sure the lane is clear before entering.,b:Check your blind spot.,c:Signal your intentions ahead of the lane change.
note: Before changing lanes, signal, check mirrors, and quickly look over your shoulder to clear blind spots.

question: What lighting should you use when driving in rainy conditions?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beams.,c:Parking lights only.
note: Use low beams in rain because high beams reflect and reduce visibility.

question: Which statement about driving on wet roads is correct?
options: a:As your speed increases, your tires become less effective on water.,b:Deep water is less hazardous than shallow water.,c:Water does not affect vehicles with good tires.
note: Higher speeds reduce a tire’s ability to clear water, which can lead to hydroplaning — when a tire rides on a film of water and loses traction.

question: What is the only effective way to reduce your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Drink coffee.,b:Exercise.,c:Allow your body time to get rid of the alcohol.
note: Only time allows your body to metabolize alcohol; coffee, exercise, or cold showers do not reduce BAC.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a traffic light turns from green to yellow as you approach an intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to beat the red light.,b:Be prepared to stop safely.,c:Apply the brakes sharply to stop immediately.
note: A steady yellow means the light is about to turn red; slow and prepare to stop if you can do so safely.

question: What is the best way to handle a driver tailgating you?
options: a:Gradually slow down or change lanes to encourage them to pass.,b:Slam on your brakes to warn them.,c:Speed up to widen the gap ahead of you.
note: Monitor rear traffic, then slow gradually or change lanes so the tailgater can pass; avoid sudden braking or speeding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching an uncontrolled intersection, you should:
options: a:Yield to vehicles coming from the right and be prepared to stop.,b:Maintain your speed and proceed without checking, c:Yield to all other drivers regardless of position.
note: At an intersection with no signs or signals yield to traffic approaching from your right and be prepared to stop to avoid a collision.

question: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings must be:
options: a:Followed only when there is other traffic.,b:Always obeyed.,c:Merely suggestions to drivers.
note: Traffic control devices govern vehicle movement and safety; you must obey signs, signals, and pavement markings.

question: When near a motorcycle, what must you allow the motorcyclist?
options: a:Allow the motorcycle to use only half of a lane.,b:Allow the motorcycle to use a complete lane.,c:Drive on the shoulder beside the motorcycle.
note: Motorcycles are full-size vehicles that require a full lane; never share a lane or crowd a motorcyclist.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To pass a slower vehicle on a two-lane, two-way road you must:
options: a:Only attempt the pass when it is legal and safe and you can use the oncoming lane to complete the pass.,b:Never cross the centerline to pass.,c:Use the shoulder to pass when it is clear.
note: Passing on a two-lane, two-way road is only allowed when it is legal and safe, and you may need to use the oncoming lane to complete the pass safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a driver's left arm is extended upward, what does that signal mean?
options: a:The driver intends to turn right.,b:The driver intends to turn left.,c:The driver plans to stop.
note: When a driver's left arm is raised upward, it signals an intended right turn; be aware of this when following.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light require you to do?
options: a:Proceed with caution.,b:Stop and wait for a green light.,c:Yield only to oncoming traffic.
note: A flashing yellow means slow down and proceed with caution; it does not require a full stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, what must you do?
options: a:Assume the guard is not supposed to be directing traffic.,b:Copy what surrounding traffic is doing, despite the guard's instructions.,c:Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.
note: Crossing guards' directions must be followed; slow down and use extra caution in school zones.

question: What is the safest way to pass a bicyclist?
options: a:Slow down and give the bicyclist as much space as possible.,b:Drive in the bicycle lane until you can pass, then merge back.,c:Honk at the bicyclist to alert them before passing quickly.
note: When passing a bicyclist, reduce speed and provide as much lateral space as possible; do not crowd or pass too fast.

question: If a green arrow for your turn changes to a solid green light, what must you do?
options: a:You may still turn, but you must first yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:You may no longer turn and must proceed straight.,c:You still have the right‑of‑way to turn without yielding.
note: When a green arrow ends and a solid green remains, you may turn in that direction but you must yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians first.

question: A steady yellow traffic signal warns that what will soon appear?
options: a:A steady red light.,b:A flashing yellow.,c:A steady green.
note: A steady yellow means the signal is about to turn red; prepare to stop safely if you can.

question: Which safety restraint combination provides the most effective protection in a crash?
options: a:Both a lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.,b:Only an airbag.,c:Only a lap belt.
note: Wearing a lap and shoulder belt together with a properly functioning airbag provides the best protection in a frontal crash.

question: When you see an emergency vehicle using its lights or siren, you must:
options: a:Pull to the right curb and stop.,b:Slow down and keep moving in your lane.,c:Keep driving in your lane and ignore the vehicle.
note: When an emergency vehicle is approaching with lights or siren, immediately pull over to the curb or edge of the road and stop to allow it to pass.

question: What should you check before switching on the ignition?
options: a:That you and all passengers have fastened seat belts.,b:That only child passengers have buckled their belts.,c:That only adult passengers have buckled their belts.
note: Develop the habit of buckling your seat belt and ensuring all passengers are belted before starting the vehicle.

question: If another driver is driving aggressively behind you, how should you react?
options: a:Stare at the driver as he or she is passing you.,b:Try to get out of the aggressive driver’s way.,c:Speed up as he or she is passing you.
note: Do everything possible to get out of the aggressive driver's way: avoid eye contact and let them pass safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two drivers arrive simultaneously to an open intersection, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on the right has the right-of-way.,b:The driver on the left has the right-of-way.,c:One may continue without stopping.
note: When two vehicles arrive at the same time, yield to the vehicle on your right; then proceed when safe.

question: If the driver behind you wants to pass, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up.,b:Slow down to allow room in front of your vehicle for the other driver to complete the pass easily.,c:Go the same speed.
note: When someone wants to pass, slow down and create space ahead so they can complete the maneuver safely and quickly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you must stop at an intersection that has no stop line or crosswalk, where should you stop?
options: a:At the point nearest the intersecting roadway where you can see approaching traffic without entering the intersection.,b:Anywhere you choose as long as you slow down, c:In the intersecting roadway to get a better view.
note: If there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop at the nearest point where you can see approaching traffic without entering the intersecting roadway.

question: If other drivers are acting angrily, what is the best way to protect yourself?
options: a:Avoid making eye contact and do not react with gestures.,b:Engage with them to calm the situation.,c:Physically and mentally distance yourself from the situation.
note: When faced with an angry driver, avoid eye contact and gestures and safely put distance between you and the other vehicle.

question: When stopped in traffic that is crossing railroad tracks with no signals or gates, what must you ensure?
options: a:You have space to fully clear the tracks without stopping.,b:You may pass slower vehicles while crossing.,c:You have the right-of-way so you do not need to check for trains.
note: Ensure you can clear the tracks completely before driving onto them. Never pass another vehicle while approaching or crossing tracks.

question: Approaching an emergency vehicle stopped with flashing lights, what must you do?
options: a:Stay in your lane and continue to drive at the same speed.,b:Slow down and, if possible, change lanes to give the stopped vehicle more room.,c:Drive to the right side of the road and stop immediately.
note: Move over a lane if safe; if not possible, slow down below the posted limit and give the stopped emergency or service vehicle as much room as you can.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering interstate traffic from an entrance or acceleration ramp, what should you do?
options: a:Has the right-of-way.,b:May force their way into traffic.,c:Yield to drivers already on the interstate.
note: Drivers entering from ramps must yield to traffic already on the interstate and merge safely when there is a gap.

question: Signs that require you to obey specific instructions are called:
options: a:Regulatory signs.,b:Warning signs.,c:Information signs.
note: Regulatory signs indicate laws or regulations that drivers must follow; violations may result in penalties.

question: If an oncoming vehicle is using high beams and fails to dim them, where should you look to avoid being blinded?
options: a:Toward the center of the road.,b:Toward the right side of the road.,c:Either side of the road.
note: If an approaching driver does not dim high beams, glance to the right edge of the road to avoid being blinded while keeping your vehicle on course.

question: What are the risks associated with worn or bald tires?
options: a:Are likely to hydroplane.,b:Can increase your stopping distance.,c:Can make turning more difficult.
